supermodules.title: Math for Physical Computing
supermodules.description: Algebra through information theory — the mathematical toolkit every layer of the stack draws from.

supermodules.title: Physics and Chemistry of Computing
supermodules.description: From atomic structure to semiconductor physics: why matter behaves the way it does inside a chip.

supermodules.title: Electricity, Electronics, and Signals
supermodules.description: Circuit laws, analog signals, noise, and the physical foundations of digital hardware.

supermodules.title: Digital Logic and Hardware Design
supermodules.description: Boolean algebra through HDLs, FPGAs, and timing closure — how logic gates become computation.

supermodules.title: Computer Architecture and Machine Execution
supermodules.description: ISA, pipelining, caches, virtual memory, and multiprocessors — the hardware a program runs on.

supermodules.title: C, Assembly, Compilers, Linking, and Binaries
supermodules.description: How source code becomes machine instructions: C semantics, toolchains, ELF, and runtime startup.

supermodules.title: Core Operating Systems
supermodules.description: Processes, scheduling, memory management, filesystems, IPC, and OS security fundamentals.

supermodules.title: Linux User Space and System Programming
supermodules.description: The Unix philosophy in practice: shells, core utilities, libc, init, and systems programming.

supermodules.title: Linux Kernel Internals
supermodules.description: The kernel source tree, syscall path, scheduler, MM, VFS, block layer, and eBPF — from the inside.

supermodules.title: Drivers and Hardware Interaction
supermodules.description: All driver frameworks: PCI, USB, I2C, SPI, input, storage, network, graphics, power management.

supermodules.title: Networking and Distributed Communication
supermodules.description: The full Linux network stack: sockets through netfilter, NIC drivers through distributed system patterns.

supermodules.title: Performance, Security, Virtualization, and Beyond
supermodules.description: Profiling, kernel security, containers, KVM, storage performance, and advanced Linux engineering.
